title: Curriculum Communication to Instructional Staff
requirement: The LEA ensures each school effectively communicates the curriculum to all instructional staff.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
items: This written process establishes the procedures GRPS will use to implement, document, monitor, and annually review compliance with Section 1: Indicator 1. It is designed to ensure the district can demonstrate both the existence of a written procedure and evidence that the procedure is implemented in practice.

sections.heading: 2. Applicability
items: This process applies to all GRPS schools, departments, programs, administrators, employees, contractors, and stakeholders whose work is subject to the indicator. Where the indicator applies only to a specific federal program or population, the process is limited to that program or population.

sections.heading: 3. Governing Requirement
items: The LEA ensures each school effectively communicates the curriculum to all instructional staff.

The district will also follow the applicable federal statute and regulations, Uniform Guidance requirements, MDE program guidance, approved grant applications, and GRPS fiscal and administrative procedures.

sections.heading: 1. Maintain a district-approved curriculum framework identifying standards, courses, instructional resources, pacing expectations, and where staff access current curriculum documents.
2. Communicate curriculum expectations to instructional staff at the beginning of the year and whenever substantive revisions occur.
3. Provide onboarding and role-specific support for new instructional staff and staff assigned to a new course or grade.
4. Document curriculum communication through agendas, attendance records, electronic communications, professional learning materials, or other dated evidence.
5. Monitor school-level access to and implementation of the district curriculum and address identified gaps through technical assistance.
6. Evidence must be contemporaneous, dated when practicable, and sufficient to show implementation rather than merely intent.
7. When implementation occurs at the school level, central-office monitoring will include a method for verifying school compliance and providing follow-up technical assistance.
8. Identified noncompliance or incomplete documentation will be assigned corrective action, a responsible person, and a completion date. Completion will be verified and documented.
9. Material changes to the process, program requirements, MDE guidance, or federal requirements will trigger an interim review rather than waiting for the annual review.
5. Documentation and Evidence to Retain
items: The current approved written process and any related forms, templates, guidance, or checklists.

Dated implementation evidence appropriate to the indicator, such as agendas, minutes, attendance records, communications, approvals, monitoring tools, reports, data analyses, fiscal records, logs, consultation records, or evaluation results.
Evidence of required stakeholder participation or consultation, when applicable.
Records of technical assistance, monitoring findings, corrective actions, and verification of resolution.
Annual review documentation showing whether the process was effective and what revisions were made.

sections.heading: 6. Internal Controls and Quality Assurance
items: Segregate initiation, approval, fiscal processing, and monitoring functions when practicable.
Use standardized forms or electronic workflows for recurring approvals and documentation.
Maintain version control so staff can identify the current approved procedure.
Periodically sample implementation records for completeness, timeliness, and consistency.
Escalate unresolved compliance issues to the appropriate district administrator and document resolution.

sections.heading: 7. Monitoring Cycle
items: At least annually, and more frequently when risk warrants, GRPS will review implementation evidence, identify gaps, verify corrective actions, and determine whether the written process requires revision. Prior to an MDE On-Site Review, the district will assemble representative evidence demonstrating implementation across the review period.

sections.heading: 8. Record Retention
items: Records will be retained for the period required by the applicable grant, federal and state requirements, audit/monitoring requirements, and the GRPS records-retention schedule. Records subject to audit, litigation, claim, or unresolved monitoring findings will be retained until the matter is resolved, even when the normal retention period has expired.

sections.heading: 9. Annual Review and Revision
items: The district will review this process annually for legal/programmatic changes, implementation issues, monitoring findings, audit results, and changes in district systems. Revisions will be communicated to affected staff and incorporated into training or technical assistance as appropriate.
